items.message:
High tides this evening may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 07:15 pm to 11:15 pm on Saturday 24th October 26. 
Flooding for Christchurch Harbour and the tidal stretches of the Lower Stour and Avon is possible for the evening tide at 9.15pm on Saturday 24/10/26.  Stormy weather systems will cause sea levels to be higher than forecasted in the tide tables.  Sea spray overtopping is possible and high-water levels in the harbour are forecast.  A level of 1.29 mAOD is expected with Force 8 South Westerly wind.  Flooding to roads and low-lying land is possible and conditions can apply two hours either side of high tide. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.   
This message will be updated by 2:30PM on Sunday 25 October or as the situation changes.

High tides on Saturday may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible for 2 hours either side of Saturday evening's tide at 23:00 on 24/10/2026. 
Storm Boelo could cause overtopping of the beach, affecting Climping Street Car Park. A small amount of water may then flow or be directed westwards along Mill Lane towards residential property in Climping Street. This event will increase tide table values by 0.26 m. Total forecast tide is 5.87 metres Chart Datum (2.82 mAOD) at Littlehampton. Strong Westerly Force 7 wind. Similar conditions will be experienced until 27th October. Sunday's tide at 11:15 on 25/10/2026 is forecast to be 10 cm lower (2.72 mAOD). 
We are closely monitoring the situation . We routinely check the condition of the beach at Climping. 
Consider activating any flood protection products you may have. Access could be restricted. Take care if visiting Climping beach. 
This message will be updated by 6:00PM on Sunday 25 October or as the situation changes.

Flooding could affect locations near the River Lim, River Char, River Winniford, Simene River, River Brit, River Asker, River Mangerton and the River Bride. Storm Boelo increases tide table values by 0.45 m. Total forecast tide is 4.52 metres Chart Datum (1.93 mAOD) at Cowes. Strong Westerly Force 6 wind. Large waves will cause spray overtopping and overwashing of defences across the exposed coast at Yarmouth, Freshwater Bay, Sandown, Shanklin, Gurnard and Ryde. This will flood esplanades, sea front car parks and roads in these locations. As Cowes is sheltered from waves, impacts, if any, will be minimal. We do not expect property flooding. We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Consider activating any flood protection products you may have.   
This message will be updated by 3:00PM on Sunday 25 October or as the situation changes.
